response: Although the cobalt blue light slit-lamp biomicroscopy method (SLBM) can be used to measure mesopic pupil size, it has some limitations. The SLBM tends to underestimate mesopic pupil size and has a wide range of agreement with other methods, such as the CIP. Additionally, it shows low sensitivity in detecting pupils larger than 6 mm, which may be misleading when planning anterior segment surgery. However, with proper training and compensation for the systematic underestimation, the accuracy of the SLBM can be improved. Therefore, while the SLBM can be used to measure mesopic pupil size, its results should be interpreted with caution and considered in conjunction with other methods for more accurate assessments.
